subject: A tough one? Box-and-Whisker plot with separated but aligned frequency plot. Faceting?

messages.author: 0a55aaf03e9d763d
messages.subject: A tough one? Box-and-Whisker plot with separated but aligned frequency plot. Faceting?
parts:
Hello everybody,
Essentially I want to add a frequency count under a box plot. Hence:

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

## test data generation
a1 <- data.frame(x=rep(1,100), y=rnorm(100, 5,1))
a2 <- data.frame(x=rep(2,75), y=rnorm(75, 3,0.5))
a3 <- data.frame(x=rep(3,133), y=rnorm(133, 12,2))
a <- rbind(a1,a2,a3)
b <- count(a, "x")

#plotting
p <- ggplot(a, aes(x=as.factor(x), y=y)) + geom_boxplot()
q <- ggplot(b, aes(x=x, y=freq)) + geom_bar(stat="identity")

# the trick I want to avoid
sidebysideplot <- grid.arrange(p, q, heights=c(3/4, 1/4), nrow=2)

The thing is that grid.arrange() does not return a plot object hence I
cannot automagically save it later using ggsave(). Pain.
Faceting obviously should come to the rescue but I have no idea how to
mix different plots in the same resulting faceted object.

Any hints?
Thanks in advance,
jcb!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: A tough one? Box-and-Whisker plot with separated but aligned frequency plot. Faceting?
parts:
Hi:

Here's one approach:

a <- data.frame(x = rep(1:3, c(100, 75, 133)),
y = c(rnorm(100, 5, 1), rnorm(75, 3, 0.5), rnorm(133, 12, 2)))

ggplot(a, aes(x=as.factor(x), y=y)) + geom_boxplot() +
geom_text(data = b, aes(x = x, y = 0.5, label = freq), size = 4) +
annotate('text', x = 0, y = 0.5, label = 'n:', size = 4) +
xlab('x')

HTH,
Dennis
